text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-Open ballot boxes arrive suddenly at Zahle serai, so it was decided to re-count votes cast at 28 polling stations in the Bekaa valley polls. Main dispute is whether education minister Ghanem has won or not.
-The 1997 public budget is more austere than the 1996 budget by 83 billion Lebanese pounds.
-Foreign Minister Bouez says after returning from Arab foreign ministers' meeting in Cairo: "The Israeli government is preparing for things other than peace".
-Committee approves the licencing applications of four television stations and 12 radio stations out of the mass of private audiovisual media outlets in Lebanon.
-Bank of Lebanon gross foreign currency reserves grew by $20.4 million in the first half of September.
-Police destroy 438 kg (964 pounds) of confiscated hashish.
-Bouez: "We expect an Israeli military operation as (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu wants to change the equations".
-Israeli forces shell and strafe areas north of the eastern sector of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
-SOLIDERE to issue Global Depositary Receipts worth $150 million through Merrill Lynch.
-Lebanese man is on trial in Germany on charges of burning down a building.
-The government will face objections over the monopoly of the audiovisual media by political chiefs resulting from the committee's decision.
-Surplus of 234 billion pounds in weekly treasury bill issue of 586 billion.
-Maronite Patriarch Sfeir hopes that the next parliamentary elections are more democratic than the 1996 polls.
